description: ENVIRONMENT: every PreToolUse hook command declared in settings.json resolves to a file that actually exists and is executable — the precondition for auditing what each hook runs, not just that a hook is registered
command: OK=1; for c in $(jq -r '.hooks.PreToolUse[].hooks[].command' .claude/settings.json 2>/dev/null); do p=$(echo "$c" | sed "s#\$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR#$PWD#"); [ -x "$p" ] || OK=0; done; [ "$OK" = 1 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: ENVIRONMENT: settings.json carries a permissions.allow list that is well-formed JSON — the baseline a supply-chain audit diffs a running session against
command: jq -e '.permissions.allow | type == "array" and length > 0' .claude/settings.json >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: ENVIRONMENT: every MCP server shipped under platform/mcp-servers/ carries a tools.json manifest declaring its read_only posture — advertised capability, not asserted trust, is what a supply-chain audit checks
command: OK=1; N=0; for m in platform/mcp-servers/*/tools.json platform/mcp-servers/*.tools.json; do [ -f "$m" ] || continue; N=$((N+1)); jq -e 'has("read_only")' "$m" >/dev/null 2>&1 || OK=0; done; [ "$OK" = 1 ] && [ "$N" -ge 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: ENVIRONMENT: dep-triage's declared tools list is missing Edit/Write, but that is prose — the deep dive's point is that only the runtime enforces it, and disallowedTools names the same two verbs so the file cannot silently drift from the enforced boundary
command: D=$(grep '^disallowedTools:' .claude/agents/dep-triage.md 2>/dev/null); echo "$D" | grep -q '"Edit"' && echo "$D" | grep -q '"Write"' && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR SUPPLY-CHAIN AUDIT: agentops/secops/supply-chain-audit.md documents every PreToolUse hook and the shell it actually executes — not just that a hook is registered
command: F=agentops/secops/supply-chain-audit.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qiE 'hook' "$F" && grep -qiE 'change-gate|deny-cluster-mutation|release-gate-secops' "$F" && echo pass || echo incomplete

description: YOUR SUPPLY-CHAIN AUDIT: the audit diffs every MCP server's advertised tool list against what its code actually exposes — provenance of a capability, not trust in its description
command: F=agentops/secops/supply-chain-audit.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qiE 'mcp' "$F" && grep -qiE 'advertise|expose|tools/list|manifest' "$F" && echo pass || echo incomplete

description: YOUR SUPPLY-CHAIN AUDIT: the audit diffs the live settings.json permissions.allow list against a known-good baseline and records any drift
command: F=agentops/secops/supply-chain-audit.md; [ -f "$F" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qiE 'permissions\.allow|settings\.json' "$F" && grep -qiE 'diff|baseline|drift|widen' "$F" && echo pass || echo incomplete
